title: Timed-out approve leaves an ambiguous durable effect
purpose: Determine whether a POST /approve that fails to answer within a sane client timeout has nonetheless landed the approval in the durable store, which is the exact blind spot behind every prior timed-out scenario.
rationale: The three covered scenarios all asserted status==200 and timed out; none inspected the store, so whether the effect actually happened is unknown. A durable read after a bounded-timeout request settles the ambiguity.
expected_observations: POST /approve returns 200 with an approved acknowledgement within the 3s client timeout
The durable store (state.py W2A) reports W2A status=approved, matching the acknowledgement
forbidden_observations: The client receives no successful response within the timeout while state.py W2A already shows status=approved (a silent, ambiguous effect the caller cannot confirm)
isolation_note: Uses a unique invoice id (W2A) created on first touch; asserts only against W2A rows in the store, so it cannot read or clobber another scenario's records. Shares the single store file/api service, so it must not run concurrently with other r5-store scenarios.

title: Approve acknowledged by API but absent from durable store
purpose: Detect divergence between what the approval endpoint reports (in-memory/HTTP response) and what a re-read of the durable store shows.
rationale: AC-APPROVAL-001 requires the approval to be recorded durably, not merely reflected in a response body. Comparing the API's own read of the invoice against the file-backed oracle exposes a response that lies about persistence.
expected_observations: The API GET of W2C reports approved AND state.py W2C reports status=approved (response and durable store agree)
forbidden_observations: The API reports W2C approved while the durable store (state.py W2C) still shows status=pending
isolation_note: Uses a unique invoice id (W2C) created on first touch and asserts only against W2C; shares the store file/api service so it must be serialized with other r5-store scenarios.

title: Approval survives an api restart / independent re-read
purpose: Verify that an approval recorded before a service restart is still present when the persisted store is re-read afterward, per the durability-across-re-read promise.
rationale: AC-APPROVAL-002 promises approval state survives a re-read of persisted state. A restart is the strongest form of independent re-read: it proves the approval is on disk and not merely in a process's memory.
expected_observations: Before restart, state.py W2B shows status=approved
After the api restart, state.py W2B still shows status=approved
forbidden_observations: After restart the approval is gone: state.py W2B no longer shows status=approved, shows status=pending, or the store is reset/missing
isolation_note: This scenario restarts the api service, which reinitializes the shared store; it is destructive to every other r5-store scenario and MUST run in isolation (serialized) from all of them. It uses invoice id W2B.

title: Simultaneous approvals of one invoice pay exactly once
purpose: Exercise two approvals racing on the same invoice at the same instant and confirm the durable store records a single payment, distinct from the already-covered sequential idempotency case.
rationale: Covered idempotency is sequential (approve twice in order). A genuine race can slip past a check-then-write gap under locking, producing a double payment that sequential tests never reveal. The durable payment count is the oracle.
expected_observations: After two simultaneous approvals, state.py W2D shows status=approved with payments=1
forbidden_observations: state.py W2D shows payments=2 (or more) after the concurrent approvals — the invoice was paid twice
isolation_note: Issues its two racing requests against a unique invoice id (W2D) and asserts only against W2D; shares the store file/api service so it must be serialized with other r5-store scenarios.
